options: Students started wasting too much food.
Students hated the lines on the food trays.
The new trays reduced a large amount of food waste.
Students brought their own lunch boxes to school.
The members of Warm Hearts were very proud of their work.
questions.question:
[지문]
One day, our school principal announced, "Our students often take too much food and waste it at lunchtime. How can we reduce food waste?"

The members of Warm Hearts gathered to solve this problem. We thought that adding lines to food trays would be helpful. Students could look at the lines and take the right amount of food.

Our school principal liked this idea, so he changed the food trays in the cafeteria. It was a success!

밑줄 친 It was a success!가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: "It was a success!"는 학교 주인공이 식판에 줄을 추가한 아이디어가 성공적이었다는 의미이며, 이는 새로운 식판이 음식물 낭비를 대량으로 감소시켰다는 내용과 일치합니다.

My sister is taller than my mom.
My sister is the tallest than my mom.
questions.question: 나의 여동생은 엄마보다 키가 크다. 주어진 우리말을 영어로 알맞게 옮긴 것은?
questions.explanation: 비교급을 사용하여 표현하며, "My sister is taller than my mom."이 "나의 여동생은 엄마보다 키가 크다"는 의미를 정확히 전달합니다.

options: (A) that  (B) were needed  (C) safely
(A) what  (B) needed  (C) safer
(A) that  (B) needed  (C) safer
(A) what  (B) were needed  (C) safer
(A) that  (B) needed  (C) safely
questions.question:
[지문]
After we solved this problem at our school, we started to look for problems in our community. We found out (A) [that / what] some roads around our school were very dark at night. We all agreed that the roads (B) [needed / were needed] more lights. With the help of a teacher, we put up lights with sensors around the neighborhood. Now all our neighbors feel (C) [safer / safely] than before!

다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) 'found out that' 구문에서 'that'을 사용합니다. (B) '도로가 불이 더 필요하다'는 능동 의미이므로 'needed'를 사용합니다. (C) 'feel'은 감각동사이므로 형용사 'safer'를 사용합니다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Have you ever used a digital kiosk before? You may think it's easy. ( ⓐ ) But some people have trouble using kiosks. ( ⓑ ) We explained every step of ordering: starting an order, choosing from the menu, and paying. ( ⓒ ) After the class, people said, "Now we feel more comfortable with kiosks. Thank you so much!" ( ⓓ ) We felt very proud. ( ⓔ )

글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

주어진 문장: To help them, we volunteered as digital guides at the community center.
questions.explanation: "To help them"은 앞의 "some people have trouble using kiosks"라는 상황을 받아서 그들을 돕기 위해 자원봉사를 했다는 내용이 이어져야 합니다. 따라서 ⓑ 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question:
[지문]
W: Welcome to the Happy Animal Shelter. Can I help you?
B: Yes. I'm here to ⓐ volunteer.
W: Can I have your name, please?
B: I'm Jinho. I love dogs, so I want to ⓑ abandon them.
W: That's great! I'll ⓒ hide our puppies first.
B: They're so cute. What should I do to help?
W: While we ⓓ clean the cage, take these puppies for a ⓔ walk, please.
B: Okay. I'm excited to spend some time with them!
W: I'm glad. Thank you for volunteering!

다음 대화의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것들로 짝지어진 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓑ 'abandon'(버리다, 포기하다)은 개를 사랑한다는 문맥에 맞지 않으며, 'care for' 또는 'help'가 적절합니다. ⓒ 'hide'(숨기다)도 문맥에 맞지 않으며, 'show'가 적절합니다.

Your actions can make _______________. Even the smallest acts can make a big difference!

주어진 글이 의미하는 바를 다음과 같이 정리할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 글은 지역사회의 문제를 해결하여 이웃들이 더 안전함을 느끼게 만든 긍정적 변화를 다루고 있으므로, 'positive changes'가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question:
[지문]
B: Hi, Julie. You look worried. Can I help you?
G: Yes, I'm looking for my phone. I think I lost it.
B: Your phone will ring when I call. I'm calling you now.
G: Ah, here it is! Thank you for helping me.
B: You're welcome.

밑줄 친 표현과 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?
questions.explanation: "Can I help you?"는 "Do you need any help?"로 같은 의미로 바꿔 쓸 수 있습니다. 둘 다 도움을 제시하는 표현입니다.

options: positive: making you feel relaxed and free from pain
principal: the person in charge of a school or college
solve: to find the answer to something or to stop a problem
volunteer: to offer to do something without being asked to do it
explain: to make something clear to understand by giving reasons for it
questions.question: 다음 중 단어와 그 영영 풀이가 잘못 연결된 것은?
questions.explanation: 'positive'의 정의가 잘못되었습니다. 'positive'는 "optimistic, confident, or favorable"의 의미이며, "making you feel relaxed and free from pain"은 'relaxing'의 정의입니다.

After the class, people said, "(A) 이제 우리는 키오스크가 더 편안하게 느껴져요. Now we feel more comfortable with kiosks. Thank you so much!" We felt very proud.

우리말에 맞춰 '이제'가 가장 먼저 오도록 영작할 것, 아래 주어진 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용하여 문장을 완성할 때, 5번째 올 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

주어진 단어: we / more / feel / with / comfortable / now / kiosks
questions.explanation: 문장 순서: "Now we feel more comfortable with kiosks." 이는 5번째 단어가 'comfortable'임을 나타냅니다.

questions.question: 다음 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.explanation: 'good'의 최상급은 'the best'이지 'the gooddest'가 아닙니다. 불규칙 형용사로 올바른 형태는 'the best day in my life'입니다.

options: a, b
a, c, d
a, d, e
b, d, e
c, d, e
questions.question:
[지문]
B: Good morning, Soye! What are you doing?
G: Hi, Ben. I'm trying to put up a poster, but it's not easy.
B: Can I help you? I can hold it for you.
G: Sure! Thank you for lending a hand.
B: You're welcome. What is this poster for?
G: It's for the Community Cleanup.
B: What is the Community Cleanup?
G: It's a volunteer activity. People sweep the streets and pick up trash to make our neighborhood clean.
B: That's a good idea! Can I join?
G: Of course! It is open to everyone.

다음 대화의 내용과 일치하는 것을 <보기>에서 모두 고른 것은?

<보기>
a. Soye is having a hard time putting up the poster alone.
b. The Community Cleanup is an activity only for students.
c. Ben starts the conversation because he is interested in the activity at first.
d. The main activity is sweeping streets and picking up trash.
e. Ben says he wants to join, and Soye says he can.
questions.explanation:
a. 맞음 - "it's not easy" (포스터를 붙이는 것이 쉽지 않음)
d. 맞음 - "People sweep the streets and pick up trash" (거리 청소와 쓰레기 줍기)
e. 맞음 - "Can I join?" "Of course!"
b. 틀림 - "It is open to everyone" (모두에게 열려있음, 학생 전용 아님)
c. 틀림 - Ben은 먼저 Soye가 포스터를 붙이는 것을 도와주려고 접근하므로 그 이후에 관심을 보임

questions.question:

Volunteering can be a great experience. I ⓐ have volunteered at the local library before. I read English books to kids ⓑ who were not good at English. ⓒ The most meaningful moment for me was seeing the smiles on the kids' faces. After volunteering, I ⓓ felt happyer because I ⓔ was able to help many kids.

밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?

questions.question:
[지문]
Have you ever used a digital kiosk before? You may think it's easy. But some people have trouble using kiosks.

To help them, we volunteered as digital guides at the community center. We explained every step of ordering: starting an order, choosing from the menu, and paying.

After the class, people said, "Now we feel more comfortable with kiosks. Thank you so much!" We felt very proud.

다음은 동아리의 리더 Yuna와의 가상 인터뷰이다. 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 답변을 한 것은?

Reporter: Why did you choose kiosks?
Yuna: We knew that kiosks are hard for some people.

Reporter: What did you teach during the volunteer work?
Yuna: We taught everything from starting an order to paying.

Reporter: What did the people say?
Yuna: They thanked us and said they felt more comfortable using kiosks.

Reporter: Did you make a book about how to use kiosks?
Yuna: No, we just explained the steps to them.

Reporter: Did your principal tell you to do this?
Yuna: Yes, he made us do this work.
questions.explanation: 기자가 교장 선생님이 이 일을 하라고 하신 거냐고 묻자, Yuna는 '네, 그분이 우리에게 이 일을 하라고 하셨어요'라고 답하고 있다. 하지만 글에서는 학생들이 키오스크 사용에 어려움을 겪는 사람들을 돕기 위해 자발적으로 디지털 가이드로 나섰다고 되어 있으므로 일치하지 않는다.
